newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise to offer 20 shrs/41 Suez in merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise to offer 20 shrs/41 Suez in merger - paper.

text.p: Newspaper Le Monde reported on Friday that the parity in a merger between utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux and holding company Cie de Suez would be 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise shares.
That exchange would take into account a special payment by Suez of 3.8 billion francs, equivalent to three times the dividend, the report said.
Both Lyonnaise and Suez declined to comment on the report in Le Monde when contacted by Reuters.
At Suez a spokeswoman reiterated that the boards of the two groups were due to meet on April 11. "It is out of the question to make any comment before this date," said a Suez spokeswoman.
The two companies have already said they are in merger talks and the stock market is now waiting for news of the terms of the alliance.

Le Monde cited "sources close to the case" as saying the talks were advanced to the stage where they "no longer concerned more than the second decimal point" of the level at which the shares are valued against each other in the deal.

It said the working base for that equation had been set at 1.94 Suez shares for each Lyonnaise share and that Suez had accepted the principle of an exceptional dividend to sweeten the deal for minority shareholders.

"According to our information, the financial company (Suez), which will annul its own self-controlled shares, is preparing to pay a normal dividend of 8.20 francs per share, in other words totalling 1.270 billion francs," it said.
"A 'premium' of 2.5 billion francs would be added to this," it said.
"In total the group would pay out 3.8 billion francs," it said.
It said this amount "appeared to be accepted by the majority of board members" and that the share parity at which the deal would be done would be adjusted to fit with the payment.
"According to the last calculations, the rate would be 2.05, in other words 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise shares," the newspaper said.

Le Monde also said the question of the board structure for the merged group also appeared to be nearing a solution where there would be a single board headed by Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod until mid-1998, with Suez boss Gerard Mestrallet as vice chairman and managing director and ready to take over the reins from mid-1998.
